nodes.title: Norm, quotient and restriction of zeta contracts
nodes.statement: Let a quotient G→G/N or an open subgroup U⊆G induce a compatible localization square; for U require Λ(G)_S finite projective over the chosen Λ(U)-localization. Quotient derived base change induces a map on relative K₀ and localized K₁; open-subgroup restriction of scalars induces the K-theory transfer. Their boundaries commute. Evaluation after quotient uses inflated representations; evaluation after transfer uses induced representations. Consequently the image of a zeta element satisfies the transported contract exactly when the arithmetic complex comparison and the normalized interpolation identities hold. For G^ab use N=[G,G] only when this quotient localization is admitted.
hypotheses: Canonical denominator/localization compatibility is proved for the chosen quotient or open subgroup.
The arithmetic base-change/restriction and normalized L-function induction identities hold, with identical Euler-factor sets and periods.
proofSteps: Use functoriality of the perfect localization fibre sequence; quotient tensor and finite-projective restriction carry the supported subcategories into the correct supported subcategories.
Apply the evaluation induction and inflation identities from NE.3.
Use the arithmetic complex comparison to identify the transported relative boundary, then compare the actual normalized interpolation values. No equality of ideals suffices for the last step.
acceptance: The identity quotient and identity subgroup induce identity maps on contracts.
For U=Γ⊆C₂×Γ, transfer evaluation at 1 equals the product of the 1 and sign evaluations.
A chosen map that sends an S-denominator to a nonunit cannot define a map from Λ_S; the theorem must refuse it.

nodes.title: Normalized abelian determinant comparison
nodes.statement: For an abelian specialization shared with IntegralIwasawaTheory I.9, compare the transported arithmetic complex and determinant trivialization, then identify the NE zeta image with that owner’s actual normalized p-adic L-function. The comparison fixes the variable γ↦1+T, arithmetic/geometric Frobenius convention, Artin dual, S-removal and T-smoothing, and any period or epsilon factors. An equality of principal ideals or Fitting ideals is only the divisor-level consequence. The stronger element-level comparison is a target with an explicit supplier gap until the normalized determinant data are provided.
hypotheses: A common abelian extension, coefficient ring, prime and local conventions in the two formulations; both arithmetic complexes are perfect and the same localization is admitted.
The imported all-prime theorem is used only in its proved hypotheses; an odd-prime result does not settle the real two-primary comparison.
proofSteps: Use derived base change and duality to identify the arithmetic determinant lines and their trivializations, retaining local correction factors.
Compare normalized interpolation formulas at a dense allowed set and invoke the exact one-variable/pseudomeasure separation theorem.
Apply the reduced-norm kernel statement only if lifting the scalar identity back to noncommutative K₁; leave every undetected kernel explicit.
acceptance: Multiplication of a power series by 1+p preserves its ideal and changes its value at T=0, detecting a comparison that proves only ideal equality.
Under γ↦1+T, replacing γ by γ⁻¹ sends T to (1+T)⁻¹−1; the normalized formula must track this substitution.
T-smoothing multiplies the L-element by the prescribed local factor; deleting it while retaining the same Selmer module fails the comparison.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for abelian × prime-to-p Galois groups
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and Gal(F_∞/F) = G × Δ, G abelian and Δ finite of order prime to p. Then MC(F_∞/F) holds, and K₁(Λ(G × Δ)) → K₁(Λ(G × Δ)_S) is injective. For G = H × Γ with H finite abelian, the Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure ζ is a unit of Λ(G)_S (Lemma 15) with ∂ζ = −[C(F_∞/F)] (Theorem 16).
hypotheses: μ = 0; p odd; #Δ prime to p.
proofSteps: Lemma 15: Λ(G)_S ≅ ⊕_{ψ∈Ĥ′} Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(H_p × Γ)_S, each summand local; (ψ × 1)(ζ) ∉ π_ψΛ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ)_S by μ = 0 and Wiles's theorem, so ζ is a unit.

Theorem 16: characterwise, ∂(ψ(ζ)) = −[C_ψ] is Wiles's main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5) for the Deligne–Ribet functions G_ψ (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3); θ₀ : K₀(Λ(G), Λ(G)_S) → ∏_ψ K₀(Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ), Λ_{𝒪_ψ}(Γ)_S) is injective, because x = |H|^{−1}Σ_h h Σ_ψ x_ψ ψ(h^{−1}) shows the cokernel of θ injects into that of θ_S (snake lemma).

Lemma 17: for p ∤ #Δ, K₁(Λ(G × Δ)_S) ≅ ⊕_{χ∈R(Δ)} Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G)_S^×, and ζ = Σ e_χ L_p(χ), with L_p(χ) built from Deligne–Ribet functions by Brauer induction (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction Layer 6), is the zeta element.
Theorem 18: K₀(Λ(G × Δ), Λ(G × Δ)_S) ≅ ⊕_χ K₀(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G), Λ_{𝒪_χ}(G)_S), and the same decomposition for K₁ gives injectivity.
acceptance: The analytic input (Deligne–Ribet) and the arithmetic input (Wiles) are imported, not reproved; μ = 0 is used for the unit property.

sources.match: Theorem 18 with Lemma 15, Theorem 16 and Lemma 17 (pp. 14–17).

nodes.title: The Burns–Kato patching principle
nodes.statement: Let 𝒞 be a family of pairs (U, V), U open in G and V closed normal in U with U/V admissible, and θ = (θ_{U,V}) : K′₁(Λ(G)) → ∏_𝒞 K′₁(Λ(U/V)), θ_S the same on the localisations, each θ_{U,V} the norm to U followed by the quotient map. Suppose θ is an isomorphism onto a subgroup Φ, θ_S lands in a subgroup Φ_S with Φ_S ∩ ∏ K′₁(Λ(U/V)) = Φ, MC holds for every F_∞^V/F_∞^U with (ζ_{U,V}) ∈ Φ_S, and every Artin character of G is a ℤ-combination of characters induced or inflated from the U/V. Then MC(F_∞/F) holds, and K′₁(Λ(G)) → K′₁(Λ(G)_S) is injective when each K′₁(Λ(U/V)) → K′₁(Λ(U/V)_S) is.
hypotheses: The hypotheses listed; μ = 0 for each subquotient.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: Choose f ∈ K′₁(Λ(G)_S) with ∂f = −[C(F_∞/F)] (boundary-surjective-p-torsion); θ_S(f) has components f_{U,V} with ∂f_{U,V} = −[C(F_∞^V/F_∞^U)] by base change (totally-real-iwasawa-complex).
u_{U,V} = ζ_{U,V} f_{U,V}^{−1} has ∂ = 0, so lies in K′₁(Λ(U/V)); (u_{U,V}) ∈ Φ_S ∩ ∏ K′₁ = Φ, so u_{U,V} = θ(u)_{U,V} for a unique u, and ζ = uf.
∂ζ = −[C]; interpolation by writing ρ = Σ n_i Ind/Inf ρ_i and using the norm and inflation compatibilities of evaluation (Kakde §2.4 (i)–(iii)); uniqueness and injectivity by the same diagram.
acceptance: This is the argument Kakde repeats in Theorems 21, 27, 33 and 36; planning it once lets each reduction supply only the description of Φ.

sources.locator: §1, the observation of Burns and Kato, p. 3 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: The principle stated in the introduction and carried out in each reduction.

nodes.title: Burns's reduction to one-dimensional extensions
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0. If MC holds for every F_∞^U/F with U ≤ H open pro-p and normal in G, and each K′₁(Λ(G/U)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G/U)_S), then MC(F_∞/F) holds.
hypotheses: μ = 0; the quotients G/U are one-dimensional.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: k1-prime (Corollary 20): K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_U K′₁(Λ(G/U)).

Uniqueness makes (ζ_{G/U}) a compatible system; burns-kato-patching with 𝒞 = {(G, U)} and Φ the inverse limit; every Artin character of G factors through some G/U, and [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] = [F_∞^U(μ_p) : F_∞^U] as U is pro-p.
acceptance: The injectivity hypothesis on K′₁ is carried, not dropped.

sources.match: Theorem 21 and its proof (pp. 19–20).

nodes.title: Reduction to ℚ_p-elementary Galois groups
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible, one-dimensional, with μ = 0. If MC holds, and K′₁(Λ(U)) → K′₁(Λ(U)_S) is injective, for every admissible subextension whose Galois group U is ℚ_p-elementary (U = P ⋊ Γ with a central open Γ^{p^r} and (P ⋊ Γ)/Γ^{p^r} an l-ℚ_p-elementary finite group C_n ⋊ P₁, the image of P₁ in (ℤ/n)^× lying in Gal(ℚ_p(μ_n)/ℚ_p)), then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K′₁(Λ(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G)_S).
hypotheses: G one-dimensional: G ≅ H ⋊ Γ with Γ^{p^e} central.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: Dress–Wall induction: K′₁(𝒪[P]) ≅ lim_π K′₁(𝒪[π]) over the K-elementary subgroups π, with norms and conjugations (Oliver, Theorem 11.2; see the gap on Oliver's book).
Lemma 26: K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ lim_P K′₁(Λ(U_P)) over the ℚ_p-elementary P ≤ G_n = G/Γ^{p^{e+n}}, U_P their preimages (k1-prime's Lemma 19 in the limit).

burns-kato-patching, with compatibility of (ζ_P) under conjugation and norms from uniqueness and the invariance of L_Σ under conjugation and induction; interpolation by Brauer's induction theorem (Tau Ceti InductionRestriction Layer 6), elementary subgroups being ℚ_p-elementary.
acceptance: Uses ℚ_p-elementary subgroups for the K₁ isomorphism, although Brauer induction needs only elementary ones.

sources.match: Theorem 27 with Definitions 23–24, Theorem 25 and Lemma 26 (pp. 20–23).

nodes.title: The l-ℚ_p-elementary case, l ≠ p
nodes.statement: If F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and G = Gal(F_∞/F) is l-ℚ_p-elementary for a prime l ≠ p, then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K₁(Λ(G)) injects into K₁(Λ(G)_S). Here G ≅ Γ^{p^e} × Ḡ with Ḡ = C ⋊ P finite (Lemma 28); reducing to C a cyclic p-group and P of order prime to p, with C̄ = H⁰(P, C), P₁ = ker(P → Aut C) and G₁ = Γ × C × P₁, the map θ = (quotient, norm) : K₁(Λ(G)) → K₁(Λ(Γ × C̄ × P)) × K₁(Λ(G₁)) is an isomorphism onto Φ = {(x₀, x₁) : norm(x₀) = can(x₁), x₁ fixed by P} (Proposition 30).
hypotheses: For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: Lemma 28: the minimal central Γ^{p^e} splits off.
If p ∤ #C, abelian-case applies. Otherwise SK₁(Λ(G)) = 1 (Oliver 12.7), and θ lands in Φ: conjugation by P preserves the norm's matrix class, and the norm square commutes.
Surjectivity: J = ker(K₁(Λ(G₁)) → K₁(Λ(Γ × C̄ × P₁))) is pro-p (Oliver 2.10; Fukaya–Kato 1.5.3), so n = (P : P₁)-th roots exist in J^P.

Injectivity: Lemma 31 (every irreducible representation is inflated from C̄ × P or induced from G₁) makes β dual to (χ, ρ) ↦ Inf χ + Ind ρ injective; Oliver–Taylor's logarithm has kernel μ_{p−1} × G^ab (Wall), which the first component detects.
Then burns-kato-patching with abelian-case for the two components.
acceptance: Oliver's and Wall's theorems are cited inputs (see the gap on Oliver's book).

sources.match: Theorem 33 with Lemmas 28, 31, Definition 29 and Proposition 30 (pp. 23–27).

nodes.title: Reduction of the p-ℚ_p-elementary case to Δ × pro-p
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and G p-ℚ_p-elementary, G/Γ^{p^e} = C_n ⋊ H_p with p ∤ n, U the preimage of H_p, and for χ ∈ Ĉ_n let U_χ = ker(U → Gal(L_χ/ℚ_p)), L_χ = ℚ_p(χ). Then K′₁(Λ(G)) ≅ ⊕_{χ∈C} K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ))^{U/U_χ} (Proposition 35), and if MC holds for each F_∞^{C_χ}/F_∞^{C_n ⋊ U_χ} with K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ)) → K′₁(Λ_{𝒪_χ}(U_χ)_S) injective, then MC(F_∞/F) holds and K′₁(Λ(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ(G)_S). This reduces the main conjecture to G = Δ × G_p with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G_p one-dimensional pro-p.
hypotheses: G p-ℚ_p-elementary; μ = 0.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: Proposition 35 at finite level is Oliver's Proposition 11.6 and Theorem 12.3(4) (gap on Oliver's book); pass to the limit with k1-prime.
Gal(F_∞^{C_χ}/F_∞^{C_n ⋊ U_χ}) ≅ C_n/C_χ × U_χ, and [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] is unchanged.
burns-kato-patching; every irreducible ρ is Ind(χρ_χ) (Serre, Proposition 25), giving interpolation.
acceptance: This reduction leaves the pro-p dimension-one case, supplied by the congruence and zeta-tuple targets in this layer.

sources.match: Theorem 36 with Remark 34 and Proposition 35 (pp. 27–30).

nodes.title: The Iwasawa algebra of a one-dimensional pro-p group as a twisted group ring
nodes.statement: In the standing dimension-one setting choose representatives hγ^a, 0≤a<p^e, of G/Z, where Z=Γ^(p^e) is central. The carry cocycle τ(hγ̄^a,h′γ̄^b)=γ^(p^e floor((a+b)/p^e)) gives an Iwasawa-specific isomorphism Λ_O(G)≅Λ_O(Z)[G/Z]^τ, using the generic twisted algebra imported from InductionRestriction Layer 7. The cocycle is symmetric and normalized at the identity; in general τ(g,g⁻¹)≠1, and the inverse of a basis element is τ(g,g⁻¹)⁻¹ times the inverse-labelled basis element. Changing the selected section gives the corresponding cohomologous presentation rather than literal equality of cocycles. Restriction gives Λ_O(U_P)≅Λ_O(Z)[P]^τ; U_P is abelian for cyclic P. For a coefficient domain put R=Λ_O(Z) and T=R∖pR. For a finite product R=∏_i R_i put T=∏_i(R_i∖pR_i), not R∖pR. With this central denominator set, both canonical localizations identify as Λ_O(G)_T=Λ_O(G)_S=Λ_O(Z)_(p)[G/Z]^τ, and their p-adic completions agree. For R=Λ_O(Z) or its localized p-adic completion the cocenter is the free R-module on Conj(G/Z), with the inherited carry convention.
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
proofSteps: Expand products of the selected section hγ^a. The integer carry is central, verifies the cocycle identity, and is symmetric; identity normalization does not imply inverse-pair normalization. Changing section conjugates the presentation by the associated central 1-cochain.

T is central and consists of regular denominators. Apply Kakde Lemma 37 componentwise in the admitted unramified coefficient rings to identify localization at T with localization at S; in each coefficient domain the finite free central algebra embeds in its total quotient. The p-divisibility intersection calculation removes common p-powers from denominators.

Lemma 43: the map is surjective, and its kernel contains the commutators because τ is symmetric; conversely an element of the kernel is Σ_{x∈Ḡ/C_g} r_{xgx⁻¹}(xgx⁻¹ − g) = Σ r_{xgx⁻¹} τ(xg, x⁻¹)⁻¹(xg·x⁻¹ − x⁻¹·xg), a sum of commutators.
Lemma 45 by restricting the presentation to U_P; Lemma 46 because U_P/Z is cyclic and Z is central.
acceptance: For Ḡ = 1 (G = Z ≅ ℤ_p) the construction is Λ_𝒪(ℤ_p) itself, and Conj Ḡ is a point.
For trivial carry the imported twisted algebra agrees with MonoidAlgebra; no separate generic twisted group ring is owned here.

nodes.title: The maps θ^G and the congruence subgroups Φ^G, Φ^G_S
nodes.statement: For P ≤ Ḡ, θ^G_P : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(U_P)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)) = Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× is the norm followed by abelianisation (just the norm when P is cyclic), θ^G = (θ^G_P)_{P≤Ḡ}, and θ^G_S, θ̂^G are the same maps on K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) and K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S). The data: ver^{P′}_P : U_{P′}^ab → U_P^ab the transfer and ϕ : U_P → U_{P^p} the transfer for cyclic P, both extended to Iwasawa algebras with Frobenius on 𝒪 (Notations 40); for [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′, the trace tr^{P′}_P, norm nr^{P′}_P and projection π^{P′}_P into Λ_𝒪(U_P/[U_{P′},U_{P′}]) (Definition 48); T_{P,P′} the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈P′/P} g̃xg̃⁻¹ on Λ_𝒪(U_P), T_P = T_{P,N_ḠP} (Definition 49); and α_P(x) = x^p/∏_{k=0}^{p−1}ω_P^k(x) for nontrivial cyclic P, where ω_P is a fixed character of order p and ω_P(g) acts by g ↦ ω_P(g)g, and α_P(x) = x^p otherwise (Definition 47). Φ^G is the subgroup of ∏_{P≤Ḡ} Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× of tuples (x_P) with M1: nr^{P′}_P(x_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(x_P) whenever [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′; M2: (x_P) is fixed by conjugation by G; M3: ver^{P′}_P(x_{P′}) ≡ x_P mod T_{P,P′} when [P′ : P] = p; M4: α_P(x_P) ≡ ∏_{P′} ϕ(α_{P′}(x_{P′})) mod pT_P for nontrivial cyclic P, over the cyclic P′ ≠ P with P′^p = P, and x_{1}^p ≡ ϕ(x_{1})∏_{P′} ϕ(α_{P′}(x_{P′})) mod pT_{1} over the nontrivial cyclic P′ with P′^p = 1. Φ^G_S and Φ̂^G_S impose the same conditions in ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S and ∏Λ̂_𝒪(U_P^ab)_S^× (Definition 51). For [P′ : P] = p and ω a nontrivial character of P′/P, nr^{P′}_P(x) = ∏_k ω^k(x) and tr^{P′}_P(x) = Σ_k ω^k(x) (Lemma 50).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
For 𝒪 = 𝒪₁ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ 𝒪_n the groups split as ⊕ Φ^G_{𝒪_i} (Remark 54), so 𝒪 is unramified in the proofs.
proofSteps: Lemma 50: in the basis 1, g, …, g^{p−1} of R[P′^ab]^τ over R[P/[P′,P′]]^τ, multiplication by x = Σ a_i g^i is the twisted circulant matrix with rows (a₀, …, a_{p−1}), (g^p a_{p−1}, a₀, …), …; the vectors (1, ω^k(g)g, …, ω^k(g^{p−1})g^{p−1}) are eigenvectors with eigenvalues ω^k(x), so the determinant and trace are the product and sum.
M4 is well posed: α_C(x) ≡ 1 mod p for nontrivial cyclic C (Remark 83), and T_P is an ideal of Λ_𝒪(U_P)^{W_ḠP}.
acceptance: The conditions are the multiplicative analogue of the pair condition of Proposition 30 (Remark 54); compare l-elementary-case.

nodes.title: The additive maps t^G_P, η_P, β^G and the group ψ^G_R
nodes.statement: Let R = Λ_𝒪(Z) or Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}. For P ≤ Ḡ, t^G_P : R[Conj Ḡ]^τ → R[P^ab]^τ is t^G_P([g]) = Σ_{x∈C(Ḡ,P)} {x⁻¹gx : x⁻¹gx ∈ P} over left coset representatives, independent of their choice. For cyclic P, η_P : R[P]^τ → R[P]^τ is the R-linear map with η_P(h) = h for generators h of P and 0 otherwise, For P≠1 this is η_P(x) = x − (1/p)Σ_k ω_P^k(x); for P=1 it is η_1=id. β^G_P = η_P ∘ t^G_P for cyclic P and t^G_P otherwise, and β^G_R = (β^G_P)_P (Definition 55). For cyclic P, T_{P,R} is the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈W_ḠP} gxg⁻¹ on R[P]^τ, W_ḠP = N_ḠP/P (Definition 56). ψ^G_R ⊂ ∏_{P≤Ḡ} R[P^ab]^τ is the group of tuples (a_P) with A1: for [P′,P′] ≤ P ≤ P′ (and [P′,P′] ≠ P if P is nontrivial cyclic), tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(a_P) if P is not cyclic, η_P(tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′})) = π^{P′}_P(a_P) if P is cyclic and P′ is not, and tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) = 0 if P′ is cyclic and P<P′ (equality imposes no vanishing); A2: (a_P)_{P∈C(Ḡ)} is invariant under conjugation by Ḡ; A3: a_P ∈ T_{P,R} for every cyclic P (Definition 57). δ = Σ_{P cyclic} δ_P : ∏_P R[P^ab]^τ → R[Conj Ḡ]^τ[1/p], δ_P(x) = [x]/[Ḡ : P], is a left inverse of β^G_R (Definition 61, Lemma 62), and β^G_R lands in ψ^G_R (Lemma 60).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
R[Conj Ḡ]^τ is only an R-module (Remark 42).
proofSteps: Lemma 60, A1: tr^{P′}_P ∘ t^G_{P′} = π^{P′}_P ∘ t^G_P, since both send [h] to [P′ : P]·h for h ∈ P and to 0 otherwise; apply η_P when P is cyclic; if P < P′ are both cyclic, β^G_{P′}([g]) involves only generators of P′, whose traces to P vanish.
Lemma 60, A2: transport coset representatives, t^G_{g₁Pg₁⁻¹}([g]) = g₁t^G_P([g])g₁⁻¹. A3: t^G_P = t^{N_ḠP}_P ∘ t^G_{N_ḠP}, and t^{N_ḠP}_P([g]) = Σ_{x∈W_ḠP} x⁻¹gx ∈ T_{P,R} for g ∈ P.
Lemma 62: for P = ⟨g⟩ and its conjugates P′, δ(β([g])) = ([Ḡ : P])⁻¹ Σ_{P′}[N_ḠP′ : P′][g] = [g].
acceptance: For Ḡ=1, β=id and ψ=R: imposing cyclic trace-zero also at P=P′ would give ψ=0 and fail this test. For Ḡ=C_p, ψ=pR×{b with identity coefficient zero}, which is abstractly R^p.

nodes.title: Kakde's additive theorem
nodes.statement: β^G_R induces an isomorphism R[Conj Ḡ]^τ ≅ ψ^G_R (Theorem 58). Moreover id_{ℚ_p} ⊗ β^G_R : ℚ_p ⊗ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ → ∏_P ℚ_p ⊗ R[P^ab]^τ is injective with image the tuples satisfying A1 and A2, and if (id ⊗ β^G_R)(a) = (a_P) with a_P ∈ T_{P,R} for every cyclic P, then a ∈ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ and a_P ∈ R[P^ab]^τ for all P (Proposition 64).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
proofSteps: Lemma 63, cyclic components: δ_P(a_P) and δ_{P′}(a_{P′}) can cancel only for conjugate P, P′, where A2 makes them equal; so δ((a_P)) = 0 gives a_P = 0 for cyclic P (the coefficients are constant on N_ḠP-orbits by A2).

Lemma 63, noncyclic components: take P′ of least order with a_{P′} ≠ 0, h₀ in its support and a maximal P ∋ h̃₀ of index p. If P is cyclic, h̃₀ generates P (otherwise A1 for P^p ⋊ C_p ≤ P′, or for {1} ≤ P′ = P × C_p, contradicts minimality), and η_P(tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′})) ≠ 0 = π^{P′}_P(a_P) contradicts A1; if P is not cyclic, the coefficient p·a_{h₀} of tr^{P′}_P(a_{P′}) contradicts A1.
δ(ψ^G_R) ⊆ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ: by A3 write a_P = Σ_{x∈W_ḠP} xb_Px⁻¹; summing δ over the conjugates of P gives [Ḡ : P]δ_P(b_P) ∈ R[Conj Ḡ]^τ.
Theorem 58: δ ∘ β = id (Lemma 62) and β(R[Conj Ḡ]^τ) ⊆ ψ^G_R (Lemma 60); δ injective on ψ^G_R gives β ∘ δ = id there.
Proposition 64 from Theorem 58 after ⊗ℚ_p; A2 puts a_P in ℚ_p ⊗ T_{P,R}, and δ recovers a from the cyclic components.
acceptance: Artin's induction theorem would give injectivity after projecting to cyclic P (Remark 59); Kakde proves injectivity directly, so no request is needed.
The cyclic test of additive-map-beta (Ḡ = C_p) is an instance.

sources.match: Theorem 58 with Lemmas 60, 62, 63 and Proposition 64 (pp. 38–42).

nodes.title: The p-adic logarithm on relative K₁ of Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: Let R = Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} and J_R the Jacobson radical of the local ring R[Ḡ]^τ. Then J_R/pR[Ḡ]^τ is nilpotent (Lemma 65). For every ideal I ⊆ J_R, Log(1 + x) = Σ_{i≥1}(−1)^{i+1}x^i/i (x ∈ I) induces a unique homomorphism log_I : K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) → (I/[R[Ḡ]^τ, I]) ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p; if I ⊆ ξR[Ḡ]^τ for a central ξ with ξ^p ∈ pξR[Ḡ]^τ, it lands in I/[R[Ḡ]^τ, I], and it is an isomorphism if moreover I^p ⊆ pIJ_R (Proposition 67). For Λ_𝒪(G), with G_n = G/Z^{p^n} and F = Frac 𝒪, the logarithms log : K₁(𝒪[G_n]) → F[Conj G_n] of Oliver kill torsion and pass to the limit, log : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → lim_n F[Conj G_n] = F⟦Z⟧[Conj Ḡ]^τ.
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
G pro-p, so R[Ḡ]^τ is local.
proofSteps: Lemma 65: over k = 𝒪/p there is an exact sequence 0 → J_R/p → Q(k⟦G⟧) → Q(k⟦Γ⟧) → 0; the kernel N of k⟦G⟧ → k⟦Γ⟧ is k⟦G⟧I_H with I_H nilpotent (H is a finite p-group), and by Lemma 37 the denominators can be taken central.

Lemma 66 (Oliver's Lemma 2.7 for twisted Iwasawa algebras): R[Ḡ]^τ is J_R-adically complete, so Log converges on 1 + I into I[1/p] (into I under the ξ-hypothesis, since then I^n ⊆ nI); Log(uv) ≡ Log u + Log v modulo U(I) = Σ_{m≥0,n≥1}(1/(m+n))[I^m, I^n] by summing the coefficients of cyclically equivalent words; under I^p ⊆ pIJ_R, Exp converges and inverts Log, and Exp([R[Ḡ]^τ, I]) ⊆ E(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) by Vaserstein's identity Exp(rx)Exp(xr)⁻¹ ∈ E(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) and successive approximation through D_k = ⟨rx − xr : rx, xr ∈ IJ_R^k⟩.

Proposition 67 (Oliver's Theorem 2.8): apply Lemma 66 to M_n(I) ⊆ M_n(R[Ḡ]^τ), compose with the trace Tr_n, note L_n([r, u]) = Tr_n(rLog(u)r⁻¹) − Tr_n(Log u) = 0, and pass to K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ, I) = GL(R[Ḡ]^τ, I)/[GL(R[Ḡ]^τ), GL(R[Ḡ]^τ, I)].
The logarithm on K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) is Oliver's finite-level one in the limit (see the gap on Oliver's book).
acceptance: Kakde notes (Remark 68) that for R = Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} it is unclear whether log_{J_R} extends canonically to K₁(R[Ḡ]^τ); only log_{J_R} is used.

sources.match: Proposition 67 with Lemmas 65–66 (pp. 42–47), Remark 68, and the limit of finite-level logarithms (p. 47).

nodes.title: The integral logarithm on K′₁ of Iwasawa algebras
nodes.statement: Let ϕ be the endomorphism of R (Frobenius on 𝒪, p-power map on Z), extended to R[Conj Ḡ]^τ by [g] ↦ [g^p] (Definition 69). Oliver–Taylor's integral logarithm L = log − (ϕ/p)log : K′₁(𝒪[G_n]) → 𝒪[Conj G_n] sits in an exact sequence 1 → μ(𝒪) × G_n^ab → K′₁(𝒪[G_n]) → 𝒪[Conj G_n] → G_n^ab → 1 with ω(Σ a_g g) = ∏ g^{tr_{𝒪/ℤ_p}(a_g)} (Oliver, Theorem 6.6); its inverse limit is L : K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ with 1 → μ(𝒪) × G^ab → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ → G^ab → 1 exact (Definition 70). On the completed localisation, with J = ker(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S → Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}) and the splitting Γ ↪ G, every x ∈ K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) is x = uy with u in the image of K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J) and y ∈ K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}) (Lemma 71); y^p/ϕ(y) ≡ 1 mod p (Lemma 72); and L(uy) = log(u) − (ϕ/p)log(u) + (1/p)log(y^p/ϕ(y)) is a homomorphism K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) → Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}[Conj Ḡ]^τ, independent of the splitting (Definition 73, Proposition 74).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
G pro-p; 𝒪 unramified, so (p) is the maximal ideal of 𝒪.
proofSteps: Definition 70: the sequences (9) for n ≥ 0 are compatible sequences of profinite groups, so the inverse limit is exact (the finite-level sequence is Oliver's; see the gap on Oliver's book).
Lemma 71: Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S is local, so its units surject onto K′₁ and 1 + J onto K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J); 1 → 1 + J → Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S^× → Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)}^× → 1 splits by Γ ↪ G.
Lemma 72: modulo p, Λ̂_𝒪(Γ)_{(p)} is the Laurent series field 𝔽_q((X)), on which ϕ is X ↦ (1 + X)^p − 1 = X^p with Frobenius on 𝔽_q, so y^p = ϕ(y).

Integrality: L(1 − v) ≡ Σ_k (v^{pk} − ϕ(v^k))/(pk) modulo the integral elements, and pk ∣ v^{pk} − ϕ(v^k) follows from p^n ∣ v^{p^n} − ϕ(v^{p^{n−1}}), proved by grouping the monomials of v^{p^n} into orbits under cyclic permutation (legitimate because τ is symmetric) and p^t ∣ r̂^{p^t} − ϕ(r̂^{p^{t−1}}).

Independence of the splitting: the finitely many splittings agree on an open A ≤ G; L is independent on the images of K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S, J_R) and K₁(Λ̂_𝒪(A)_S), whose product has torsion cokernel in K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S), and the target is torsion free.
acceptance: Kakde leaves the kernel and cokernel of L on K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S) open (Remark 75, citing Ritter–Weiss); only the homomorphism is planned.

nodes.title: The additive and multiplicative sides: β^G(L(x)) through θ^G(x)
nodes.statement: Define v^G_P on ∏_C F⟦Z⟧[C^ab] by v^G_P((x_C)) = Σ_{P′} ([P′ : P′^p]/[P : P′^p])ϕ(x_{P′}) over cyclic P′ with P′^p ≤ P when P is not cyclic, and Σ_{P′ ≠ P′^p = P} [P′ : P′^p]ϕ(x_{P′}) when P is cyclic (Definition 78); and u^G_P on ∏_C Λ_𝒪(U_C^ab)^× by u^G_P((x_C)) = ∏_{P′^p ≤ P} ϕ(x_{P′})^{|P′|} for noncyclic P and ∏_{P′ ≠ P′^p = P} ϕ(x_{P′}) for cyclic P, over cyclic P′ (Definition 80). Then for x ∈ K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)): β^G_P(L(x)) = (1/(p²|P|))log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))^{p|P|}/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) for noncyclic P; β^G_P(L(x)) = (1/p)log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) for nontrivial cyclic P; and β^G_{1}(L(x)) = (1/p)log(α_{1}(θ^G_{1}(x))/(ϕ(θ^G_{1}(x))u^G_{1}(α(θ^G(x))))) (Proposition 84); the same holds on K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S). The logarithms are defined: α_P(θ^G_P(x))^{p|P|} ≡ u^G_P(α(θ^G(x))) mod p for noncyclic P (Lemma 82), and the cyclic quotients are ≡ 1 mod p (Remark 83).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
proofSteps: Lemma 76: log ∘ θ^G_P = t^G_P ∘ log (Oliver, Theorem 6.8); in the completed case from log(u) = lim p^{−n}(u^{p^n} − 1) and θ̂^G_P(u) = lim (1 + t^G_P(u^{p^n} − 1))^{1/p^n}.
Lemma 77: log ∘ α_P = pη_P ∘ log for nontrivial cyclic P, since ω_P commutes with log and η_P = (1/p)(p − Σ_k ω_P^k).
Lemma 79: β^G_P ∘ ϕ = v^G_P ∘ β^G for P ≠ {1}, and β^G_{1} ∘ ϕ = (ϕ + v^G_{1}) ∘ β^G, by counting cosets.
Lemma 81: log ∘ u^G_P = |P|·v^G_P ∘ log for noncyclic P and (1/p)·v^G_P ∘ log for cyclic P, by naturality of log.

Lemma 82: modulo p, α_C(θ^G_C(x)) ≡ 1 for nontrivial cyclic C and θ^G_P(x)^{|P|} ≡ θ^G_{1}(x), the latter by Schneider–Venjakob, Proposition 2.3 (on K₁(𝔽_p⟦H⟧), the norm to an open normal N followed by the inclusion is x ↦ x^{[H:N]}).

Proposition 84 by chaining Lemmas 76, 77, 79 and 81. On the completed ring write x = uy (Lemma 71): u is handled identically; for y ∈ Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)}, θ^G_P(y) = y^{[Ḡ:P]}, α_P(θ^G_P(y)) = 1 for nontrivial cyclic P and β^G_P(L(y)) = [Ḡ : P]L(y) or 0; a general y has ϕ^r(y) ∈ Λ̂_𝒪(Z)_{(p)} and y^{p^r}/ϕ^r(y) ≡ 1 mod p, and the targets are torsion free.
acceptance: At Ḡ = 1 both sides are (1/p)log(x^p/ϕ(x)).

sources.match: Proposition 84 with Lemmas 76, 77, 79, 81, 82, Definitions 78, 80 and Remark 83 (pp. 51–58).
Proposition 2.3 continues: K₁(Ω(H)) → K₁(Ω(N)) → K₁(Ω(H)), the norm followed by the canonical map, is x ↦ x^{[H:N]}, with Ω = 𝔽_p⟦−⟧. This is the input to Kakde's Lemma 82.

nodes.title: The multiplicative sequence for Φ^G
nodes.statement: θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) ⊆ Φ^G and θ̂^G_S(K′₁(Λ̂_𝒪(G)_S)) ⊆ Φ̂^G_S (Lemma 85). The map μ(𝒪) × G^ab → ∏_P Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×, (ζ,g)↦(ζ^[G:U_P]·ver^G_(U_P)(g))_P, with the scalar norm exponent and the group transfer in each component, is injective and commutes with θ^G (Lemma 86). There is a surjection ω : ψ^G → G^ab, ω_ψ=ω_A∘δ, using the additive inverse δ:ψ^G≅Λ_O(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ, with ω ∘ β^G = ω (Lemma 87). The map ℒ = (ℒ_P) : Φ^G → ψ^G, with ℒ_P((x_C)) given by the right-hand sides of Proposition 84 with x_C in place of θ^G_C(x), sits in an exact sequence 1 → μ(𝒪) × G^ab → Φ^G → ψ^G → G^ab → 1 (Lemma 88).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
proofSteps: Lemma 85, M1: the norm to U_P equals the norm to U_{P′} followed by nr^{P′}_P after abelianising, because the bases agree. M2: the norm is conjugation-equivariant.

Lemma 85, M3: write x = Σ x_k g^k over Λ_𝒪(U_P) for g ∈ U_{P′} ∖ U_P; the norm is the determinant of the twisted circulant matrix, whose terms not fixed by σ = conjugation by g cancel modulo T_{P,P′}, and Σ_h a_h^p ∏_k σ^k(h) ≡ Σ_h ϕ(a_h)∏_k σ^k(h) = ver^{P′}_P modulo T_{P,P′}.
Lemma 85, M4: by Proposition 84 and Lemma 60, pβ^G_P(L(x)) = log(α_P(θ^G_P(x))/u^G_P(α(θ^G(x)))) ∈ pT_P, and log : 1 + pT_P ≅ pT_P.
Lemma 89: if C^p ⊆ P′ but C^p ⊄ P with [P′ : P] = p, then nr^{P′}_P(ϕ(α_C(x_C))) = 1, by Lemma 50.
ℒ lands in ψ^G: A1 by cases (P not cyclic; P cyclic and P′ not, using α_P(ϕ(α_C(x_C))) = 1 unless C^p = P; P′ cyclic by Lemma 89) from M1; A2 and A3 from M2 and M4; integrality from Proposition 64.

Correct the first map to θ∘ι: the component of a scalar ζ is ζ^[G:U_P], since a scalar acts on a free module of that rank; the group component is the ordinary transfer. The top component identifies μ(O)×G^ab inside Λ_O(G^ab)^×, proving injectivity. The other end is ω_ψ=ω_Aδ and is surjective because ω_A is surjective and δ is the inverse additive isomorphism.

Kernel, cyclic components: log is injective on 1+pΛ_O(U_P), since p is odd. Descend from maximal nontrivial cyclic P in the defining ℒ equations to obtain α_P(x_P)=1 for every nontrivial cyclic P. At P=1 obtain x_1^p=ϕ(x_1), not α_1(x_1)=1. The integral logarithm for the abelian group Z therefore gives x_1∈μ(O)×Z. For successive nontrivial cyclic P, M1 and α_P=1 give x_P^p=x_(P^p), viewed by inclusion, hence x_P^{|P|}=x_1.

Kernel, finite-level input and limit: for each abelian A=U_P^ab and finite quotient A_n=A/image(Z^{p^n}), the finite integral-log exact sequence identifies the kernel with μ(O)×A_n. Compatibility and compactness give ker L_A=μ(O)×A. Since the additive target of L_A is Z_p-torsion-free, Λ_O(A)^×/(μ(O)×A) is torsion-free. The cyclic power relation puts x_P in μ(O)×U_P. For noncyclic P its defining equation gives x_P^{p²|P|}=ϕ(x_1)^p after all nontrivial α_C have become 1, and gives x_P∈μ(O)×U_P^ab by the same torsion-free quotient argument. This uses the separately named finite integral-log supplier, not a torsion-unit assertion about completed group units.

Kernel, trace rigidity: along any index-p inclusion P≤P′, write x_P=ξh and x_(P′)=ζg. M3 compares ξh with ζ^p ver(g). In every finite quotient U_P^ab/image(Z^{p^n}), augmentation and distinct Teichmüller residues imply ξ=ζ^p. The difference of the two remaining basis units is invariant under P′/P. Its support has at most two elements, so odd p makes each element fixed individually; coefficients on fixed elements in an index-p trace are divisible by p. Thus the difference is zero. Passing through the finite quotients proves x_P=ζ^p ver(g) exactly. An index-p subgroup chain from Ḡ to P recovers θ∘ι of x_Ḡ, with the scalar exponent [Ḡ:P].

Cokernel, untruncated abelianization: let π_ab be the projection of the additive conjugacy module to Λ_O(G^ab). Prove π_abδℒ(x)=L_(G^ab)(x_Ḡ). If Ḡ is cyclic, M1 identifies x with θ(x_Ḡ), and δℒθ=δβL=L. In particular do not replace δ by the generator-truncated top β component.

Cokernel, noncyclic calculation: work in Q_p⊗Λ_O(G^ab), put m=|Ḡ|, A_C=log α_C(x_C) for cyclic C (A_1=p log x_1), and U=Σ_(C cyclic)|C|ϕ(A_C). Since a∈ψ and Ḡ is noncyclic, its top β component is untruncated and equals π_abδa. The additive inverse gives π_abδa=m⁻¹Σ_(C cyclic)|C|a_C. For a=ℒ(x), substitution yields (pΣ|C|A_C−U)/(p²m); the untruncated top component is log x_Ḡ−U/(p²m). Equality of these two expressions forces Σ|C|A_C=pm log x_Ḡ; applying ϕ gives U=pmϕ(log x_Ḡ). Thus π_abδℒ(x)=log x_Ḡ−ϕ(log x_Ḡ)/p. Here log denotes the rational logarithm of the preceding logarithm construction; no unsupported power-series logarithm of an arbitrary unit is introduced.

Exactness at ψ: ω_A factors through π_ab and ω_(G^ab)L_(G^ab)=1, so ω_Aδℒ=1. Conversely, if ω_Aδa=1, the integral-log exact sequence gives z∈K′₁(Λ_O(G)) with Lz=δa. Then ℒθz=βLz=a. Products of coefficient domains take products of this entire argument. The five-lemma ladder now uses proved corrected maps and this kernel/cokernel reconstruction.
acceptance: For p=3 and O unramified of degree 2, let ζ have Teichmüller order 8. A rank-3 norm sends ζ to ζ³≠ζ; the scalar embedding cannot be the identity in every component.
For G=Γ, Z=Γ^p and a=z=γ^p, β_(C_p)(a)=0 while ω_A(a)=z. Recovering ω from only a_(C_p) is false; ω_Aδ retains it.
The kernel contains γ of infinite order. For O=∏_i O_i take ∏_i(μ(O_i)×G^ab), not μ(O)×a single G^ab.
At a noncyclic P, ker ℒ gives a power of x_P in μ(O)×U_P^ab; it need not make x_P torsion. The torsion-free quotient supplied by the integral logarithm is the inference required here.

sources.match: The corrected statement and kernel/cokernel reconstruction replace the defective scalar embedding and cokernel computation; E21–E22 retain the original-version findings.

The abelianized logarithm, torsion-free quotient and trace-rigidity proof provide the replacement route. Their α_Z=x_Z^p/ϕ(x_Z) absorbs the extra central factor that Kakde writes separately; their untruncated top map must not be identified with cyclic β_Ḡ.

nodes.title: Kakde's congruence description of K′₁
nodes.statement: Let G be a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with G/H ≅ ℤ_p, Z ≤ G central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, and 𝒪 the integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p or a finite direct sum of such rings. Then θ^G induces an isomorphism K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ Φ^G (Theorem 52); θ^G_S maps K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) into Φ^G_S, and Φ^G_S ∩ ∏_{P≤Ḡ} Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× = θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) (Theorem 53).
hypotheses: G is a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group with a closed normal H, G/H ≅ Γ ≅ ℤ_p, a fixed lift G = H ⋊ Γ, Z = Γ^{p^e} open in Γ and acting trivially on H (so Z is central), Ḡ = G/Z, and U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ; p is odd; 𝒪 is the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Finite products are handled componentwise, taking products of the entire groups and exact sequences, including separate G^ab factors.
proofSteps: Reduce to 𝒪 unramified over ℤ_p (Remark 54).

Theorem 52: the five lemma on the ladder μ(𝒪) × G^ab → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → Λ_𝒪(Z)[Conj Ḡ]^τ → G^ab (integral-logarithm) over μ(𝒪) × G^ab → Φ^G → ψ^G → G^ab (phi-integral-log-sequence), with θ^G, β^G (an isomorphism by additive-theorem) and the identities as vertical maps; the squares commute by Lemmas 86–87 and ℒ ∘ θ^G = β^G ∘ L (theta-beta-relation).
Theorem 53: θ^G_S lands in Φ̂^G_S ∩ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S = Φ^G_S (Lemma 85 on the completed ring), and Φ^G_S ∩ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× = Φ^G, which is θ^G(K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G))) by Theorem 52.
acceptance: Source-qualified: G pro-p of dimension one and 𝒪 unramified. The general one-dimensional G reaches this case through reduction-to-p-elementary, with 𝒪 = ℤ_p[Δ] ≅ ⊕_χ 𝒪_χ.
Checked on Ḡ = 1 and Ḡ = C₂ in congruence-group-phi's tests.

sources.match: Theorems 52 and 53 (p. 36) with their proofs (p. 65).

nodes.title: K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) injects into K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S)
nodes.statement: Let G be a compact p-adic Lie group with a quotient G/H ≅ ℤ_p, and 𝒪 the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p. Then the map K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) is injective (Corollary 90).
hypotheses: G compact p-adic Lie with G/H ≅ ℤ_p; 𝒪 unramified.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: G pro-p of dimension one: θ^G_S composed with K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) → K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S) is θ^G followed by the injection ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^× ↪ ∏Λ_𝒪(U_P^ab)^×_S, and θ^G is injective (Theorem 52).

G of dimension one: reduction-to-qp-elementary, l-elementary-case and reduction-to-p-elementary each carry the injectivity of K′₁ → K′₁ of the localisation from their subquotients to G; they end at Δ × G_p with 𝒪[Δ] ≅ ⊕_χ 𝒪_χ unramified, which is the pro-p case.

Arbitrary dimension: if x ↦ 1 in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)_S), then for every open U ≤ H normal in G and pro-p its image in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)_S) is 1, hence its image in K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)) is 1 by the dimension-one case, and x = 1 because K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G)) ≅ lim_U K′₁(Λ_𝒪(G/U)) (k1-prime, Corollary 20).
acceptance: The source prints the corollary without a proof (p. 65). The route above is reconstructed and flagged. It runs the §4 reductions with 𝒪 = ℤ_p, as printed; a larger unramified 𝒪 needs the same reductions over 𝒪, which Kakde does not write out.

sources.match: Corollary 90, stated after the proofs of Theorems 52–53; no proof is printed.

nodes.title: The main conjecture as congruences between abelian zeta functions
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be admissible with μ = 0 and Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G, with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; fix Z ≤ G central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z. For P ≤ Ḡ put F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P} and K_P = F_∞^{[U_P,U_P]}, so that Gal(K_P/F_P) = Δ × U_P^ab, and let ζ_P ∈ Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)^×_S be the Deligne–Ribet (Cassou-Noguès, Barsky) p-adic zeta function of K_P/F_P (Notations 91). Then MC(F_∞/F) holds if and only if (ζ_P)_P ∈ Φ^G_S, where Φ^G_S = Φ^G_{ℤ_p[Δ],S} (Proposition 93). Every irreducible Artin representation ρ of G has a one-dimensional χ inflated from Γ with ρ ⊗ χ trivial on Z (Lemma 92).
hypotheses: F_∞/F admissible, μ = 0, p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G as stated.
proofSteps: Lemma 92 by induction on |G/Z|: by Clifford (Serre, Proposition 24) either ρ|_Z is isotypic, and χ = χ_i^{−1} works, or ρ = Ind_A^G η for a proper A ⊇ Z, and a χ for η on Γ^{p^r} extends to Γ.

If: take f ∈ K′₁(Λ(Δ × G)_S) with ∂f = −[C(F_∞/F)] (boundary-surjective-p-torsion). By Theorem 53, θ_S(f) = (f_P) ∈ Φ^G_S. Since ∂ζ_P = ∂f_P = −[C(K_P/F_P)] (abelian-case and base change of C), u_P = ζ_Pf_P^{−1} lies in K′₁(Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)), and (u_P) ∈ Φ^G_S ∩ ∏Λ(Δ × U_P^ab)^× = θ(K′₁(Λ(Δ × G))) (Theorem 53); with θ(u) = (u_P) (Theorem 52), ζ = uf has ∂ζ = −[C(F_∞/F)].

Interpolation: for irreducible ρ choose σ by Lemma 92, so ρ ⊗ σ factors through the p-group Ḡ and equals Ind_{U_P}^G η for some P ≤ Ḡ (Serre, Theorem 16: representations of supersolvable groups are monomial); then ρ = Ind_{U_P}^G(η ⊗ σ^{−1}) and ζ(χρκ^r) = ζ_P(χησ^{−1}κ^r_{F_P}) = L_{Σ_P}(χησ^{−1}, 1 − r) = L_Σ(χρ, 1 − r) by inductivity of Artin L-functions.
Only if (not printed): if ζ satisfies MC, the components of θ_S(ζ) interpolate the same values as the ζ_P, hence equal them, so (ζ_P) = θ_S(ζ) ∈ Φ^G_S by Theorem 53.
acceptance: The printed proof gives the 'if' direction; the converse is the standard argument and is flagged as reconstructed.
This is burns-kato-patching with Φ = Φ^G, Φ_S = Φ^G_S and the pairs (U_P, [U_P, U_P]).
The zeta-tuple-in-phi target reduces MC to M1–M4. The zeta-tuple-m1-m2, basic-congruences and m4-from-basic-congruences targets supply the four conditions.

sources.match: Notations 91, Lemma 92 and Proposition 93 with its proof (pp. 66–67), and the statement of Theorem 94 (p. 67).

nodes.title: The abelian zeta functions satisfy M1 and M2
nodes.statement: In the setting of main-conjecture-congruence-criterion, the tuple (ζ_P)_P satisfies M1: nr^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′}) = π^{P′}_P(ζ_P) in Λ(Δ × U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}])_S whenever [P′, P′] ≤ P ≤ P′; and M2: gζ_Pg^{−1} = ζ_{gPg^{−1}} in Λ(Δ × U_{gPg^{−1}}^ab)_S for every g ∈ G (Proposition 95).
hypotheses: As in main-conjecture-congruence-criterion.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: M1: for an irreducible Artin representation ρ of U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}], a character χ of Δ and r divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], nr^{P′}_P(ζ_{P′})(χρκ^r) = ζ_{P′}(χ Ind_{U_P}^{U_{P′}}(ρ)κ^r) = L_{Σ_{P′}}(χ Ind ρ, 1 − r) = L_{Σ_P}(χρ, 1 − r) = π^{P′}_P(ζ_P)(χρκ^r).
Two elements of the abelian Λ(Δ × U_P/[U_{P′}, U_{P′}])_S interpolating the same values on this dense set of characters are equal.
M2: (gζ_Pg^{−1})(χρκ^r) = ζ_P(χ gρg^{−1} κ^r) = L_Σ(χ Ind_{U_P}^G(gρg^{−1}), 1 − r) and ζ_{gPg^{−1}}(χρκ^r) = L_Σ(χ Ind_{U_{gPg^{−1}}}^G ρ, 1 − r), and the two induced representations agree.
acceptance: M3 is the index-p case of the full Möbius congruence. M4 is supplied by the independent completed construction and canonical descent; no claim about validity of Kakde v3 (12) is required.

sources.match: Proposition 95 and its proof (pp. 67–68).

nodes.title: Partial zeta values and the smoothed values Δ^u_P
nodes.statement: For j ≥ 0 and a coset x of Z^{p^j} in Δ × U_P^ab, δ(x) is its characteristic function and ζ(δ(x), s) = Σ_𝔞 δ(x)(g_𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} (Re s > 1, over integral ideals 𝔞 of F_P prime to Σ_P, g_𝔞 the Artin symbol) is the partial zeta function; by Klingen and Siegel it continues meromorphically with a simple pole at s = 1 only, and ζ(δ(x), 1 − k) ∈ ℚ for even k ≥ 2. For a locally constant ε = Σ ε(x)δ(x) with values in a ℚ-vector space V, L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) = Σ_x ε(x)ζ(δ(x), 1 − k) ∈ V (15); for a degree-one Artin character it is the Σ_P-truncated L-value. For ε locally constant ℚ_p-valued, u ∈ U_P^ab and k divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], Δ^u_P(ε, 1 − k) = L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) − κ(u)^k L_{Σ_P}(ε_u, 1 − k) with ε_u(g) = ε(ug) (16). These values are invariant under conjugation: Δ^u_P(δ(y), 1 − k) = Δ^u_{gPg^{−1}}(δ(gyg^{−1}), 1 − k) for u ∈ Z, g ∈ G (Lemma 103).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: L_{Σ_P}(ε, 1 − k) is well defined: refining j splits δ(x) into the δ of its sub-cosets, and ζ is additive in δ.

Lemma 103: for Re s > 1, ζ(δ(gyg^{−1}), s) = Σ_𝔞 δ(y)(g_{𝔞^g})N(𝔞^g)^{−s} = ζ(δ(y), s) by reindexing 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞^g, and meromorphic continuation carries the equality to s = 1 − k; δ(y)_u = δ(u^{−1}y) and u ∈ Z is central.
acceptance: The Klingen–Siegel rationality and continuation are cited inputs, requested with the Deligne–Ribet package from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3.

sources.match: The definitions (15) and (16) of §6.3 and Lemma 103 of §6.5.

nodes.title: Finite-level approximations of the abelian zeta functions
nodes.statement: Let f be such that κ^{p−1}(Z) = 1 + p^fℤ_p. For P normal in P′ let T_{P,P′,j} be the image of x ↦ Σ_{g∈P′/P} gxg^{−1} on ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}), T_{P,j} = T_{P,N_ḠP,j} (Definition 100). Then Λ(Δ × U_P^ab) ≅ lim_j ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}), and T_{P,P′} ≅ lim_j T_{P,P′,j} (Lemma 101). For u ∈ U_P^ab, j ≥ 0 and k divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞], the image of (1 − u)ζ_P in ℤ_p[Δ × U_P^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+j}) is Σ_x Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k}x mod p^{f+j}; in particular the limit does not depend on k (Proposition 102, attributed to Ritter–Weiss).
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Lemma 101: a compatible family (x_j) lifts canonically — for t ≥ j the images of x_t in ℤ_p[Δ × U^ab/Z^{p^j}]/(p^{f+t}) converge to x̃_j — and the x̃_j form an element of the limit; for T_{P,P′} pass to the limit in 0 → ker(tr_{P,P′,j}) → ℤ_p[…]/(p^{f+j}) → T_{P,P′,j} → 0, exact on the right because the groups are finite.
Step 1: the sums form an inverse system, since κ(x)^k ≡ κ(y)^k mod p^{f+j} when x ↦ y.

Step 2: independence of k is congruence (17), Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k} ≡ Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k′)κ(x)^{−k′} mod p^{f+j}; with η locally constant, η^{[F_∞(μ_p):F_∞]} ≡ κ^{[F_∞(μ_p):F_∞]} mod p^{f+j}, and ε_k = p^{−f−j}η^{−k}δ(x), the function ε_kκ^{k−1} − ε_{k′}κ^{k′−1} is ℤ_p-valued, so Deligne–Ribet Theorem 0.4 applies.

Step 3: ζ_u = lim_j(Σ_x Δ^u_P(δ(x), 1 − k)κ(x)^{−k}x) satisfies ζ_u(κ^kε) = Δ^u_P(ε, 1 − k) = (1 − u)ζ_P(κ^kε) for all locally constant ε, by the Deligne–Ribet construction of ζ_P; so (1 − u)ζ_P = ζ_u.
acceptance: The Deligne–Ribet congruences (their Theorem 0.4) and the interpolation property of ζ_P are imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3.

nodes.title: Smoothed Möbius values and trace ideals
nodes.statement: In the finite-extension setting of basic-congruence-values, let λ̃_F=2^{−[F:Q]}λ_{F,S}. Fix g first. If its smoothed value congruences hold for that same g for every even locally constant ε, then the image of s_g=Σ_F μ_Σ(Σ_F) ver_F^L((1−g_F)λ̃_F) in Z_p[[H_S^+]] lies in tr_Σ(Z_p[[H_S^+]]). Here H_S^+ is the maximal totally real quotient of H_S. This is an implication from the explicit stabilizer-modulus congruences, rather than the earlier list (18), (22), (24), (28), (29).
hypotheses: p odd; finite totally real p-extension L/K; same S, transfers, Möbius coefficients, normalization and g_F as in basic-congruence-values.
The Deligne–Ribet finite-level approximation of each smoothed pseudomeasure holds.
The quantifier is one fixed g for all ε. The conductor-dependent construction in basic-congruence-values by itself gives no such uniform g.
proofSteps: Choose cofinal admissible Σ-stable finite quotients H_S/V, with V containing complex conjugations and with cyclotomic precision exceeding all [L:F] exponents plus v_p(|Σ|). The transfer kernels are included before taking a finite quotient; no injectivity of a global transfer is assumed.
The coefficient of y is c_y=N_L(y)^{−k} Σ_F μ_Σ(Σ_F) Δ̃_{g_F}(1−[L:F]k, δ_y∘ver_F^L), using N_F(x)^{[L:F]}=N_L(ver_F^L x). If y is not in the image of a transfer the corresponding function is zero.

Conjugation carries the term for F to the term for its conjugate, so s_g is Σ-invariant. Apply the value congruence to δ_y, which is even on this quotient, to obtain c_y divisible by |St_Σ(y)|. An invariant element in a finite permutation group ring is a trace precisely when its orbit coefficient is divisible by that stabilizer order.

The approximation initially gives this assertion modulo a power of p at least |Σ|. The residual invariant multiple of |Σ| is also a trace. Pass to the inverse limit of the finite trace images; compactness of the integral group rings supplies compatible trace preimages.
acceptance: For Σ=C_p and a fixed y, trace membership demands coefficient divisibility by p; for a free orbit it only demands constant coefficients on the orbit.
The factor 2^{−[F:Q]} is retained until its Möbius-weighted removal in basic-congruences; it is not removed termwise by an unsupported equality.
The statements ∀ε ∃g and ∃g ∀ε cannot be interchanged. Compactness of trace preimages applies after g has been fixed; it does not supply a common g from conductor-dependent choices.

sources.locator: §1, Proposition 4 and its full coefficient argument, pp.5–6
sources.match: The value modulus is exactly the finite permutation-module trace modulus.

nodes.title: Hilbert Eisenstein series, restriction along the diagonal and the q-expansion principle
nodes.statement: For L totally real of degree r, Hilbert modular forms of weight k on Γ₀₀(𝔣) have standard q-expansions c(0, f) + Σ_μ c(μ, f)q^μ_L over totally positive μ ∈ 𝒪_L (§6.6). For L′ ⊇ L of relative degree r′=[L′:L], restriction along the diagonal R_{L′/L} maps M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣𝒪_{L′})) to M_{r′k}(Γ₀₀(𝔣)) with c(μ, R_{L′/L}f) = Σ_{tr(ν)=μ} c(ν, f) (§6.7), and its constant term at the cusp of α is that of f at α^* (Lemma 109). For β ∈ 𝒪_L totally positive with 𝔣 ⊆ β𝒪_L, the Hecke operator U_β has c(μ, f|U_β) = c(μβ, f) (Lemma 110). Deligne–Ribet: for locally constant ε on Gal(L_Σ/L) and even k ≥ 2 there is G_{k,ε} ∈ M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣)) with q-expansion 2^{−r}L(ε, 1 − k) + Σ_μ(Σ_{𝔞∋μ} ε(g_𝔞)N𝔞^{k−1})q^μ and constant term N^k((α))2^{−r}L(ε_g, 1 − k) at the cusp of α (Proposition 111); the q-expansion principle: if f ∈ M_k(Γ₀₀(𝔣), ℚ) has non-constant standard coefficients in ℤ_(p), then c(0, f) − N(α_p)^{−k}c(0, α, f) ∈ ℤ_p (§6.11); hence c(0, G_{k,ε}) − N(α_p)^{−k}c(0, α, G_{k,ε}) = 2^{−r}Δ^u(ε, 1 − k) when α has Artin symbol u (Remark 112).
hypotheses: L totally real; Σ a finite set of finite primes containing those above p; 𝔣 an integral ideal supported on Σ.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: Lemma 109: (R_{L′/L}f)|α = R_{L′/L}(f|α^*), and constant terms are read off at τ → i∞.
Lemma 110: U_β is the double coset of diag(β, 1), f|U_β(τ) = N(β)^{k/2−1}Σ_b f|(1 b; 0 β), and the character sum Σ_b e^{2πi tr(μb/β)} is N(β) for μ ∈ β𝒪_L and 0 otherwise.
Proposition 111 and the q-expansion principle are Deligne–Ribet (Proposition 6.1, 2.22, 0.3 and 5.13–5.15); Remark 112 combines them with N((α))^kN(α_p)^{−k} = κ(u)^k.
acceptance: Deligne–Ribet's Eisenstein series, their constant terms at cusps and the q-expansion principle are requested from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3, which the atlas makes their owner.

sources.locator: §§6.6–6.11, Lemmas 109–110, Proposition 111 and Remark 112, pp. 77–81 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: The Hilbert-modular toolkit of §§6.6–6.11; Lemmas 109 and 110 are proved in the text, Proposition 111 and the q-expansion principle are cited to Deligne–Ribet.

nodes.title: The transfer into a maximal cyclic subgroup misses its generators
nodes.statement: Let P ∈ C(Ḡ) be such that no P′ ∈ C(Ḡ) has P′^p = P, and let P ⊊ N ≤ N_ḠP. Then the image of the transfer ver : N^ab → P is a proper subgroup of P (Lemma 114).
hypotheses: Ḡ a finite p-group.
For the Kakde theorem route, p is odd, as in the source’s standing assumption. Toy algebra calculations at 2 do not extend the theorem to 2.
proofSteps: For g∈N, put m=ord(gP) in N/P, the length of each orbit on N/P (P is normal in N). With one representative x_j per ⟨g⟩-orbit, transfer is ∏_j x_j⁻¹g^m x_j. The order of g itself is not the orbit length.
If g∉P and g^m generated P, then ⟨g⟩ would be cyclic with a cyclic subgroup above P whose p-th powers equal P, contradicting maximality. Thus every factor lies in P^p and their product does too.
If g ∈ P, ver(g) = ∏_{x∈N/P} x^{−1}gx; N acts trivially on the order-p subgroup of P, so ver(g)^{p^{r−1}} = ∏ g^{p^{r−1}} = g^{p^{r−1}[N:P]} = 1 for #⟨g⟩ = p^r, since p divides [N : P].
acceptance: Used in Proposition 115: nontrivial stabilisers kill δ(y)(g_𝔟).

sources.match: Lemma 114 and its proof.

nodes.title: Möbius-weighted Hilbert Eisenstein value congruences
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a finite p-extension of totally real number fields, Σ=Gal(L/K), and S contain p and every ramified finite prime. Put Σ_F=Gal(L/F), g_F=ver_K^F(g), and use the smoothed values of 2^{−[F:Q]}ζ_{F,S}, denoted by Δ̃. For every positive even k and even locally constant Z_(p)-valued ε on H_S=Gal(L_S/L), the special g constructed below satisfies Σ_{K⊆F⊆L} μ_Σ(Σ_F) Δ̃_{g_F}(1−|Σ_F|k, ε∘ver_F^L) ∈ |St_Σ(ε)| Z_(p). Here μ_Σ(V)=μ(1,V) is the subgroup-poset Möbius coefficient and even means factoring through the maximal totally real quotient. This replaces the unsupported cyclic-overgroup sum of Kakde v3 (12); it is not a claim to repair that false sum by changing weights.
hypotheses: p odd; L/K and S as in the statement. No μ=0 hypothesis is needed for this finite analytic congruence.

Choose a common conductor ideal f supported on S, divisible by |Σ|, for all ε∘ver_F^L. Choose a positive rational integer f₀∈f, and the rational finite idèle α with components 1+f₀ at primes dividing f₀ and 1 elsewhere. Let γ=α_K and g=Art_K(γ). Then γ and γ⁻¹ lie in 1+f̂ and N_F(g_F)=(1+f₀)^{−[F:Q]}, so every g_F has nontrivial cyclotomic image.
proofSteps: For each intermediate field form G_{[L:F]k, ε∘ver_F^L}, restrict from F to K, then apply U_[F:K]. The common weight is [F:K][L:F]k=[L:K]k, and the q^a coefficient sums over (β,b) with β∈b⊆O_F, b prime to S and Tr_{F/K}(β)=[F:K]a. Keep these relative degrees; an absolute degree from a different bottom field cannot replace them.

Identify these pairs with the Σ_F-fixed pairs in L. Because S includes every ramified prime, an invariant ideal prime to S descends to the fixed field. For a pair with stabilizer P≤Σ the full subgroup sum contributes ε(b)N_L(b)^k Σ_{V≤P} μ_P(V) r^[P:V], where r=N_L(b)^(−1/|P|) is a rational p-unit, obtained by descending b to L^P. This uses every subgroup V≤P with its multiplicity.

For P≠1 take the Teichmüller lift z of r modulo p. Then r^{p^n}≡z modulo p^{n+1}. The finite p-group Möbius identity gives |V| divides p μ_P(V): μ(1,V)=0 unless V is elementary abelian, and for rank d its value is (−1)^d p^{d(d−1)/2}. This identity is a finite subgroup-poset induction using the Frattini quotient and the Gaussian-binomial recursion; include that combinatorial lemma in the supplier proof, not an analytic assumption. Each summand is congruent to μ_P(V)z modulo |P|. Their sum vanishes since Σ_{V≤P} μ_P(V)=0. For P=1 the required modulus is 1 and the assertion is automatic.

Group pairs under St_Σ(ε). An orbit has |St_Σ(ε)|/|St_Σ(ε)∩P| elements, while its single-pair contribution is divisible by |P|, hence by |St_Σ(ε)∩P|. Every nonconstant coefficient of the Möbius sum E is divisible by |St_Σ(ε)|.

Use only the special cusp γ above. The matrix diag(γ,γ⁻¹) belongs to the completed level group, so its second factor M₂ in the Deligne–Ribet cusp decomposition is the identity. Thus applying U_[F:K] preserves the constant coefficient at this cusp, by its standard-cusp coefficient formula. This proves the required Hecke comparison at these cusps; no arbitrary-cusp assertion is used.

The normalized cusp expansion multiplies the constant coefficient by N_K(g)^{[L:K]k}=N_F(g_F)^{[L:F]k}. Therefore the constant coefficient of E(1)−E(γ) is exactly the stated sum of Δ̃ values, including each smoothing exponent and each relative weight. The q-expansion principle transfers the nonconstant-coefficient divisibility to this constant difference.
acceptance: For Σ=C_p×C_p the coefficients are 1 at 1, −1 at each of the p+1 lines, and p at Σ. At p=3 and r=2 the stabilizer polynomial is 2^9−4·2^3+3·2=486, divisible by 9. Replacing the full Möbius sum by an unweighted sum of cyclic overgroups fails this test.

For a proper normalizer N in a larger finite quotient, restriction to its fixed field multiplies a weight by [N:P], not [Ḡ:P]. The special-cusp norm identity must use the same bottom field as that restriction.
For the full stabilizer P=1 no cancellation Σμ=0 is asserted: divisibility modulo 1 is enough. For P≠1 retain all fixed pairs, including β rational and b=O_L.

sources.locator: Propositions 5 and 9, pp.6–9; Lemma 10 and conclusion, pp.10–11 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: Relative restriction weights, complete stabilizer sums and the special-cusp Hecke calculation prove the stated value congruence.
Comparison only: this revision does not use the cyclic-overgroup sum, its fixed-pair cancellation, or the omitted proof of (29). See E33–E34.

nodes.title: Analytic Möbius and index-p transfer congruences
nodes.statement: Let G be a one-dimensional p-elementary totally real Galois group, A an abelian normal open subgroup containing its prime-to-p cyclic factor, and Q=G/A. In the central localization Λ•A, Σ_{A≤U≤G} μ_Q(U/A) ver_A^{U^ab}(ζ_{U^ab}) belongs to tr_Q(Λ•A), with the same S-truncation on every abelian pseudomeasure. For |Q|=p this is the index-p transfer congruence M3. In the finite-over-cyclotomic pro-p setting, central localization by central elements regular modulo p agrees with the canonical S-localization; unramified coefficient factors are treated componentwise.
hypotheses: p odd; totally real extension finite over the cyclotomic tower; S contains p and all ramified primes.

Use abelian pseudomeasures with the Deligne–Ribet normalization; μ=0 is required when viewing them as units in the completed/canonical main-conjecture construction, not for the finite analytic value congruence.
proofSteps: Use Ritter–Weiss Congruences II, Theorem p.2, for a single g with nontrivial cyclotomic transfer in every intermediate field and with the smoothed Möbius sum in the trace ideal. The coefficient reduction is basic-congruence-reduction; basic-congruence-values explains the conductor-dependent Hilbert calculation. Its per-function choice of cusp does not by itself prove the theorem’s uniform existence assertion. That precise source-theorem input remains an independent proof-audit obligation below. Work on the universal abelian S-ramified groups and their totally real quotient, with L the fixed field of A.

Remove the tilde normalization in the Möbius sum. For V=Gal(L/F), the difference μ_Q(V)(2^{−[F:Q]}−2^{−[L:Q]}) is divisible by |Q|. Indeed |V| divides p μ_Q(V), and for V≠1 the factor (2^{|V|−1})^{[F:Q]}−1 has p-adic valuation at least 1+v_p([F:Q]); for V=1 the difference is zero. Its invariant sum is a trace. This only uses the p-primary modulus, not divisibility modulo [F:Q].

Put h=ver_K^L(g). Each summand has the common factor 1−h. Localize the universal group ring only at Z_p[[closure〈h〉]]∖p, then map to Λ•A. The cyclotomic image of h is nontrivial, so 1−h becomes a unit there. This is the deflation of a pseudomeasure in Ritter–Weiss Lemma c; it also works when A has a prime-to-p factor. The entire universal augmentation localization need not map to that factor and is not used.

The transfer/deflation square follows from corresponding coset representatives in G(L_S/K) and its quotient G. Divide the smoothed sum by the Q-fixed unit 1−h after this square; trace ideals commute with this central localization. This proves the displayed ordinary-pseudomeasure congruence.
To obtain Kakde M3 for P≤P′ of index p, apply the index-p case to U_{P′}/[U_P,U_P], whose normal subgroup U_P^ab is abelian. The full G need not itself be abelian.
acceptance: For Q=C_p this gives ζ_A−ver_A^{G^ab}(ζ_{G^ab}) in tr_Q, with the sign determined by μ_Q(Q)=−1.

Kakde v3 (12) is not a target: take Ḡ=C_{p²}×C_p, P=pC_{p²}×0. There are p cyclic P′ with P′^p=P, and W_Ḡ(P) has order p² acting trivially. M3 implies ζ_P≡φ(ζ_{P′}) modulo p for each P′, whereas (12) would imply ζ_P≡pζ_P=0 modulo p, contradicting that ζ_P is a unit. The corrected full Möbius sum preserves the missing multiplicity.
Retain the uniform existence assertion of the named theorem, not a deduction of ∃g ∀ε from ∀ε ∃g. No claim is made that the conductor-dependent calculation alone discharges this assertion.

sources.locator: Proposition 6, p.3; §3, Lemma c and (3.1)–(3.3), pp.10–12
sources.match: Normalization removal, legitimate pseudomeasure deflation and division by the common smoothing factor.

sources.locator: Theorem, p.2, and concluding Remark, p.11
sources.match: The special-g congruence and the limitation on universal localization with a prime-to-p factor.

nodes.title: The auxiliary extension F̃_∞ and the trace-ideal bound
nodes.statement: Choose a prime l ≡ 1 mod |Ḡ| with ℚ(μ_l) ∩ F_∞ = ℚ, let K ⊆ ℚ(μ_l) have degree |Ḡ| over ℚ, and put F̃ = KF, F̃_∞ = F̃F_∞. Then Gal(F̃_∞/F) = H̃ × Δ × G with H̃ cyclic of order |Ḡ|, and G̃/Z ≅ H̃ × Δ × Ḡ. For P ∈ C(G̃) let i_P = max{[P′ : P] : P ⊆ P′ ∈ C(G̃)}. If P ≠ {1} then T_P ⊆ p·i_P²·Λ(Δ × U_P), and T_{1} = |G̃|Λ(Δ × Z); the same holds for T_{P,S} and T̂_P (Lemma 118). The main conjecture for F̃_∞/F implies it for F_∞/F.
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Case P ⊆ H̃: i_P = [H̃ : P] and N_{G̃}P = G̃ acts trivially on Λ(Δ × U_P), so T_P = [G̃ : P]Λ = |Ḡ|[H̃ : P]Λ ⊆ p·i_P²Λ since |Ḡ| ≥ p·i_P.
Case P ⊄ H̃: P = ⟨(h̃, h)⟩ with h ≠ 1; for P′ = ⟨(h̃₀, h₀)⟩ realising i_P, H̃ × ⟨h₀⟩ ⊆ N_{G̃}P acts trivially, so T_P ⊆ (|H̃||⟨h₀⟩|/|P|)Λ = |H̃|i_PΛ ⊆ p·i_P²Λ as |H̃| ≥ p·i_P.

Admissibility and μ = 0 for F̃_∞, which the source asserts without argument (E10): K is totally real because |Ḡ| is odd and divides (l − 1)/2, and μ = 0 passes from F_∞ to the finite p-extension F̃_∞ (the vanishing of μ is inherited by finite p-extensions, a theorem of Iwasawa, cited here).
Descent: MC for F̃_∞/F gives MC for its quotient F_∞/F by the compatibility of ∂, C and interpolation with the quotient map (as in reduction-to-dimension-one).
acceptance: The descent along G̃ → G uses Fukaya–Kato's base change for C, recorded in the gap on Fukaya–Kato.

sources.match: The trick of §6.13, the field F̃_∞ and Lemma 118 with its proof.

nodes.title: Descent of a completed zeta element to the canonical localization
nodes.statement: Let A_G=Λ_O(G), with G one-dimensional pro-p, finite kernel over Γ, central open Z≅Z_p and O an unramified coefficient domain. Let B_G be the p-adic completion of the central-regular localization of A_G. If b∈K₁(B_G) has abelianized norms equal to the normalized abelian zeta functions ζ_P, then there is ζ∈K′₁((A_G)_S) with θ_S(ζ)=(ζ_P) and ∂ζ=−[C]. In particular that tuple satisfies M1–M4. The result uses abelian main conjectures and arithmetic base change to impose its boundary; it does not identify the Ritter–Weiss refined class with [C].
hypotheses: p odd; finite-over-cyclotomic totally real μ=0 setting; A_G and C as in the canonical main-conjecture criterion.
The integral θ-isomorphism K′₁(A_G)≅Φ, the inclusion θ̂(K₁(B_G))⊆Φ̂, the surjective canonical localization boundary, and the abelian main conjectures with base change of C are available.
All denominator sets and coefficient products are componentwise. For Δ×G, apply the argument to the unramified domains O in Z_p[Δ].
proofSteps: Choose f∈K′₁((A_G)_S) with ∂f=−[C], and representatives in K₁ when mapping to B_G. The base-change boundary square and the abelian main conjecture give u_P=ζ_P/θ_S(f)_P∈Λ_O(U_P^ab)^×. Abelian semilocal K₁ is its unit group, so this asserts integrality of the element and its inverse.

The ratio b/f_B has completed θ-image u, so u∈Φ̂. Prove the contraction Φ̂∩∏_P Λ_O(U_P^ab)^×=Φ. Put R=O[[Z]], and R̂ the p-completed localization of R at R∖pR. The map R/p^n→R̂/p^n is injective: a denominator nonzero modulo p is a non-zero-divisor successively on p^i/p^{i+1}. All rings in the θ-diagram are finite free over R.

For a trace condition let W act on U_P^ab, with Z embedded centrally. Its finite coset set U_P^ab/Z admits W-equivariant lifts: a coset stabilizer acts on a lift by a homomorphism to the torsion-free group Z, and its finite image must be zero. Choose lifts orbit by orbit. In this permutation R-basis the trace image on an orbit is generated by |St_W(v)| times the orbit sum. Thus trace membership is exactly coefficient divisibility by a power of p, which contracts under R→R̂; the same holds for p times the trace ideal. The embedding of Z is valid because [U_P,U_P] lies in the finite cyclotomic kernel.

M1 and M2 contract by injectivity. M3 contracts by the preceding trace computation. M4 contracts by that computation for pT, since the α and Frobenius products of integral units are integral. This proves the intersection, without inventing a map B_G→(A_G)_S or calling completed group units torsion.

Lift u to z∈K′₁(A_G) by the integral θ-isomorphism. Then ζ=zf has θ-image ζ_P and boundary −[C]. Its image under θ_S lies in Φ_S by the algebraic image theorem. Uniqueness is the separate main-conjecture criterion.
acceptance: If W acts trivially with |W|=p^a, the trace ideal is exactly p^a times the ring; completion cannot weaken this modulus.
For a free W-orbit the trace generator is its orbit sum with coefficient 1. No false divisibility by |W| is imposed.

The lift f is generally not integral and b need not come from a canonical localized element by an inverse completion map. The correction z is integral because its entire tuple u, including inverses, is integral.

sources.locator: Lemma 85, pp.58–60; Theorems 52–53, p.36, proved pp.64–65; Proposition 93, pp.66–67 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: Completed image inclusion and integral θ lifting; the contraction/boundary patching above supplies the comparison.
The same equivariant permutation-basis argument over a central procyclic subgroup.
Comparison of A(G), B(G) and the additive/multiplicative images; no unstated inverse completion map.

nodes.title: M4 from Möbius congruences and canonical descent
nodes.statement: In the one-dimensional Δ×pro-p, odd-p, totally real μ=0 setting, the normalized abelian zeta tuple satisfies M4 in the canonical localization. This is proved through the full Möbius congruences, the independent Ritter–Weiss completed construction and completed-zeta-canonical-descent. The branch through Kakde v3 Proposition 98 and Lemma 119 is replaced; it is not an assumption of this result.
hypotheses: p odd; totally real extension finite over the cyclotomic tower; S contains p and all ramified primes.
μ=0; abelian main conjectures, arithmetic base change and the corrected algebraic θ-image theorem; unramified coefficient factors treated separately.
proofSteps: The analytic and algebraic full Möbius congruences feed the Ritter–Weiss logarithmic integrality/support-reduction proof. Its torsion correction yields b∈K₁(B_G) with Det b=L, without assuming any Kakde M4 theorem for zeta functions.
Normalized abelian restriction identifies θ̂_P(b)=ζ_P for every P. Apply completed-zeta-canonical-descent to obtain ζ∈K′₁(Λ_O(G)_S) with that tuple and the required boundary.

The algebraic inclusion θ_S(K′₁(Λ_O(G)_S))⊆Φ_S, already proved independently of arithmetic congruences, gives M4. At nontrivial cyclic P it reads α_P(ζ_P)/∏_{P′^p=P, P′≠P} φ(α_{P′}(ζ_{P′}))∈1+pT_{P,S}. At P=1 the numerator is ζ_1^p/φ(ζ_1), rather than the nontrivial-character definition of α_1.

There is no dependency on zeta-tuple-in-phi or kakde-main-theorem in the completed construction or descent comparison, so this route does not use the desired arithmetic M4 to prove itself. No auxiliary-extension trace denominator is needed for this replacement.
acceptance: The C_{p²}×C_p test in basic-congruences excludes the old cyclic-overgroup sum. M4 here follows from an actual completed multiplicative preimage and contraction of integral trace conditions.
The special central P=1 factor is retained, while scalar torsion is embedded with norm powers [G:U_P].

sources.match: Independent completed multiplicative construction from full Möbius congruences, including torsion information.
Algebraic image inclusion supplies M4 after descent, independently of the rejected analytic (12).

nodes.title: The abelian zeta functions satisfy M1–M4
nodes.statement: For the original one-dimensional Δ×pro-p extension, the tuple (ζ_P) lies in Φ_S: M1–M2 follow from interpolation and conjugation, M3 from the index-p Möbius congruence, and M4 from the completed construction and canonical descent. The same statement applies to the separate enlarged extension. The canonical-localization main conjecture follows from the congruence criterion.
hypotheses: F_∞/F is admissible with μ = 0 and p odd; Gal(F_∞/F) = Δ × G with Δ cyclic of order prime to p and G a one-dimensional pro-p p-adic Lie group; Z ≤ G is central open pro-cyclic, Ḡ = G/Z, U_P ≤ G the preimage of P ≤ Ḡ, F_P = F_∞^{Δ×U_P}, d_P = [F_P : F], r_P = [F_P : ℚ], Σ_P the primes of F_P above Σ, and ζ_P the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta function of the abelian extension with group Δ × U_P^ab (Notations 91).
proofSteps: Use zeta-tuple-m1-m2 and basic-congruences for M1–M3.
Use m4-from-basic-congruences, with the replacement proof through completed-zeta-canonical-descent, for M4.
Apply the independent algebraic main-conjecture-congruence-criterion. The separate enlarged-extension descent remains valid but is unnecessary for this Möbius-based argument.
acceptance: This proves the target asserted in Kakde Theorem 94 by a replacement analytic branch; it does not validate Proposition 98 or its claimed fixed-pair cancellation.

sources.match: Theorem 94 (M1–M4, whose M4 display is a quotient, as the page image shows) and its proof assembled in §§6.2–6.13.
Independent completed construction used in the replacement proof.

nodes.title: The main conjecture for totally real fields (Kakde)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and F_∞/F an admissible p-adic Lie extension satisfying μ = 0, with G = Gal(F_∞/F). There is a unique ζ(F_∞/F) ∈ K′₁(Λ(G)_S) with ∂(ζ(F_∞/F)) = −[C(F_∞/F)] and ζ(F_∞/F)(ρκ^r_F) = L_Σ(ρ, 1 − r) for every Artin character ρ of G and every r ≥ 1 divisible by [F_∞(μ_p) : F_∞] (Theorem 11). That is, MC(F_∞/F) of NE.5/totally-real-main-conjecture holds.

nodes.title: Ritter–Weiss logarithmic pseudomeasure
nodes.statement: In the one-dimensional Ritter–Weiss setting, let Λ^G be the p-adic completion after inverting central elements regular modulo p, Q^G its total quotient, and T(R)=R/[R,R]_add the additive commutator quotient. The reduced-trace character map Tr identifies T(Q^G) with the admissible character-function space. Define t_(K/k) by Tr(t)=L(L_(K/k)), where L(f)(χ)=p⁻¹ log(f(χ)^p/Ψ(f(ψ_pχ))) and Ψ is induced by γ↦γ^p. For p-elementary G the integral group logarithm satisfies Tr∘L=L∘Det and has image in T(Λ^G). This completion and this t are distinct from the canonical localization and a multiplicative zeta element.
hypotheses: p odd; K/k totally real, k/Q finite and K/k_cyc finite; the stated character functions satisfy Galois and cyclotomic twisting compatibilities.
For integrality of the group logarithm use p-elementary G=C×P with C finite cyclic of order prime to p and P pro-p.
proofSteps: Import reduced trace and the additive commutator quotient; form the central localization and p-adic completion.
Use the reduced-trace character isomorphism to define t uniquely.
Use the integral logarithm square and Adams/Frobenius normalization from Ritter–Weiss diagram (D1); its earlier-paper inputs are recorded as a gap.
acceptance: For an abelian group, T(Λ^G)=Λ^G and the trace comparison is the scalar character comparison.
For the group-like unit γ, p⁻¹log(γ^p/Ψγ)=0; a logarithm omitting Ψ fails this test.
For the scalar unit 1+p over Z_p, the logarithm is (1−p⁻¹)log(1+p), not the ordinary log.
The zero additive pseudomeasure is uniquely determined by zero trace but does not imply uniqueness of a multiplicative preimage when SK₁ survives.

nodes.title: Möbius–Wall and abelian pseudomeasure congruences
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian normal open subgroup of p-elementary G and Q=G/A a finite p-group. For ε∈(Λ^G)^×, Σ_(A⊆U⊆G) μ_Q(U/A) ver_A^U(res_U^G ε) lies in tr_Q(Λ^A). The same Möbius sum with the abelian pseudomeasures λ_(K^[U,U]/K^U) lies in the corresponding trace ideal in the central localization Λ•A. Here res denotes the K₁ transfer before the abelian group-transfer map ver, and μ_Q is the subgroup-poset Möbius function. These are distinct algebraic and analytic congruences.
hypotheses: p odd; one-dimensional totally real Ritter–Weiss setting; A includes the prime-to-p cyclic direct factor.
The analytic clause uses the S-truncated abelian pseudomeasures and their Deligne–Ribet congruences.
proofSteps: For the algebraic clause, expand the restriction determinant using representatives of G/A and the associated group-extension cocycle. For each coset permutation group the coefficients into orbits under Q. Its cocycle factor is invariant under the permutation stabilizer (Ritter–Weiss §2, Lemma a and the claim after (2.5)).

The remaining stabilizer sum is the Möbius sum in §2 Lemma b. Prove that lemma by induction on subgroup order: split a coefficient as e₀+e₁, expand into functions on the coset set with values in {0,1}, and group nonconstant functions by their proper stabilizers. Their contributions are iterated traces by induction; constant functions cancel against the two pure terms. This retains all subgroups and conjugacy multiplicities.

For the analytic clause use basic-congruences, whose Hilbert coefficient and special-cusp calculation is supplied above, with the uniform smoothed theorem retained as a precisely stated primary-source input. The algebraic and analytic sums have the same subgroup indexing and target trace ideal; neither is the unweighted cyclic-overgroup sum of Kakde (12).
acceptance: If Q=C_p, μ_Q(1)=1 and μ_Q(Q)=−1, giving the norm-transfer difference in the Q-trace ideal.
If Q=C_p², the subgroup Möbius coefficients are 1 on 1, −1 on each line and p on Q.
If A=G, the trace ideal is all Λ^A; the resulting congruence imposes no extra condition.

nodes.title: Ritter–Weiss logarithmic integrality criterion
nodes.statement: Under the odd-prime, totally real, one-dimensional Ritter–Weiss hypotheses and μ_(K/k)=0, existence of Θ∈K₁(QG) with Det Θ=L_(K/k) and ∂Θ=℧_(K/k) is equivalent to L_(K/k)∈Det K₁(Λ^G). After p-elementary reduction, this is equivalent to t_(K/k)∈T(Λ^G). The implication from integral t to a multiplicative preimage requires the torsion congruence; the logarithm alone loses torsion information. The refined class ℧ is not silently identified with −[C] without the requested arithmetic comparison.
hypotheses: p odd; K/k totally real, k/Q finite, K/k_cyc finite; finite S contains all archimedean and ramified primes; μ_(K/k)=0.
For the second equivalence use p-elementary G and the source’s compatible character-function space.
proofSteps: Use Wiles’s abelian main conjecture to identify the localization boundary in the central-completion reduction.
Apply character induction to reduce to p-elementary G.
Use the integral logarithm square for the easy implication; for the converse isolate the torsion correction and kill it using the index-p torsion congruence.
acceptance: A torsion character function may have zero logarithm; zero logarithm alone does not put it in Det of the integral K₁.
The μ=0 hypothesis is retained when moving the boundary problem to the central completed localization.
